en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having the most perfect cone shape among all volcanoes in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 500 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley region.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird of the country and is endemic only to the forested mountains of Mindanao.
Mount Apo, located in Mindanao, is the highest mountain in the Philippines with an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Lake Lanao in Marawi City is the largest lake in Mindanao and the second-largest lake in the entire Philippines.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
The Philippine Trench, located within the Philippine Sea, reaches a maximum depth of over 10,000 meters near the islands of Mindanao.
The province of Surigao del Norte is a major producer of nickel, making the Philippines a top global nickel supplier.
Because it lies along the Pacific typhoon belt, the Bicol region frequently experiences strong tropical cyclones between June and November.
Palawan is called the last ecological frontier of the Philippines because it hosts numerous endemic species found nowhere else on Earth.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO site protecting over 600 fish species and 360 coral types.
Taal Volcano in Batangas features Main Crater Lake, which is a body of water located directly inside the volcano's main crater.
